hypothesis: The prior two-buffer asynchronous candidate was correct but slower than the synchronous control. This contrasting three-slot ring prefetches up to two future K stages while retaining the 16×16 CTA, lane-to-data mapping, scalar FP32 compute mapping, and output operation. It tests whether deeper lookahead hides more copy latency, while its extra shared memory and buffer-reuse barrier may instead worsen performance; no gain is claimed before measurement.
notes: The catalog reports two distinct valid programs: the synchronous control measured 0.01730756 s and the prior two-buffer async version 0.02106704 s. This candidate changes pipeline depth rather than merely renaming the earlier async implementation. All new performance and correctness conclusions remain for the controller to measure.
transformations: Retained the 16×16 CTA, (ty,tx) cooperative A/B staging map, scalar FP32 accumulation, and alpha/beta output expression.

Replaced two shared-memory stages with a three-slot ring and preloaded up to two future K stages using cp.async groups; wait_group keeps the current stage ready while allowing later groups to remain outstanding.
Added a CTA synchronization before reusing a ring slot, zero-filled invalid row, column, and K-tail entries, and kept a synchronous fallback for architectures below sm_80.
Preserved the run entry point, default-stream launch, input/output buffers, and absence of extra allocations.
